column5: A degradation ladder stepping down from the primary model to a fallback model, cached answers, retrieval-only results, rules and templates, and finally an honest message with a queued task or a human, triggered by health signals or a feature flag and chosen per feature.

E-commerce search with an offline lane where an LLM enriches the catalogue into BM25 fields and vectors, and an online lane where query understanding feeds hybrid BM25 and embedding retrieval, a merge with stock filters, and a learning-to-rank model trained on clicks, carts and purchases.

An AI gateway whose stateless data plane runs auth and policy, token budgets, guardrails, a cache and a router with fallback before calling hosted providers or a self-hosted pool, logging metering and redacted records, with config cached from a separate control plane.

A multi-tenant chatbot platform where channels are mapped to a tenant ID by auth, pass per-tenant quotas into a shared orchestrator fed by versioned tenant config and non-overridable platform guardrails, and every retrieval, tool, model and metering call carries the tenant ID, with namespaces for small tenants and dedicated indexes for large ones.

A batch meeting summariser: consent check, job queue, ASR with diarisation, speaker-to-attendee mapping, one LLM call for summary, decisions and actions, and verification of quotes and timestamps before delivery, with action items shown as objects carrying owner, task, due date, timestamp and quote.

A notification prioritiser where critical alerts are sent immediately and all other candidates are scored for open and disable probability and importance, then a per-user budget decides to send, add to an LLM-written digest, or not send, with the value formula shown below.

Infrastructure anomaly detection in three stages: streaming per-series detectors and log-template clustering detect, correlation with the service graph and change events groups anomalies into one incident, and only then an LLM explains it with cited evidence for the on-call engineer, whose labels feed back.

A financial document pipeline: encrypt and classify, OCR, schema-bound extraction with source spans, then reconciliation and tamper checks, where passing values go to core systems and failures go to maker-checker review, with every step written to an immutable audit trail.

A dynamic pricing engine: competitor and sales data feed a demand model and causal elasticity estimates, an optimiser proposes prices that pass through guardrails and a randomised experiment layer before publishing, big moves go to human review, and a chart shows the margin-maximising price between the floor and the cap.

Resume screening that parses and redacts each application, matches it requirement by requirement against the agreed job requirements with quoted evidence, ranks with explanations for a recruiter who makes every decision, and feeds adverse impact monitoring back into the matching.

A voice assistant split into an on-device side, where a wake word, VAD and on-device ASR with intent handle simple commands, and a cloud side, where an LLM with tools handles complex requests, confirms risky actions, and speaks through streaming TTS.

A multi-agent workflow on a durable runtime: an orchestrator plans the task as a graph, two specialist agents write to typed shared state, a reviewer agent checks outputs and can send rework back, and a human approval gate precedes the result.

Real-time transcription where clients stream audio through a sticky gateway to GPU workers that drop silence, batch one chunk per stream, and run streaming ASR under lag monitoring, then post-processing returns partials and finals to clients and stores final transcripts.

Live-stream moderation where chat and risk-sampled frames and audio pass through fast classifiers, uncertain or high-reach cases escalate to a VLM, all feed a sliding-window stream risk score, and that score triggers graduated actions directly or through human moderators.
